findings.problem: LedgerWorkflow uses raw String for status and bool flags for lifecycle, allowing illegal state combinations (e.g., is_sent=true with status != "sent", or is_validated=false after mark_sent). The compiler cannot enforce valid transitions.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can construct or mutate a LedgerWorkflow into an invalid state (e.g., is_sent=true but status="pending"), breaking auditability and ledger integrity.
findings.fix: Replace status:String with an enum type LedgerStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent } and replace is_validated/is_sent bools with a single LedgerStatus field. Make mark_sent accept only the pre-transition typestate.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool is a primitive lifecycle flag. Combined with is_sent: bool and status: String, it creates a 3-field lifecycle that can describe impossible states (e.g., validated but not sent, or sent with status="pending").
findings.failure_mode: State machine inconsistencies are only catchable at runtime via manual checks. No compile-time guarantee of valid transitions.
findings.fix: Collapse into a single enum: pub enum LedgerStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }. Remove is_validated and is_sent entirely.

findings.problem: id: String is a primitive domain identifier with no domain constraints. No validation that the id conforms to ledger ID rules (length, format, uniqueness).
findings.failure_mode: Invalid IDs (empty, malformed, duplicated) propagate into the core without rejection at the boundary.
findings.fix: Wrap in a newtype: pub struct LedgerId(String). Add a fallible constructor LedgerId::try_from(raw: String) that validates domain rules.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes a fully-constructed LedgerWorkflow and mutates it unconditionally. It does not enforce that the ledger was in a valid pre-sent state (e.g., Validated). Any state can transition to sent.
findings.failure_mode: A pending or already-sent ledger can be marked sent without validation, corrupting the audit trail and bypassing required prior steps.
findings.fix: Use typestates: pub struct LedgerPending { ... } and pub struct LedgerSent { ... }. mark_sent accepts LedgerValidated and returns Result<LedgerSent, TransitionError>, rejecting invalid transitions at compile time.

findings.problem: mark_sent is a pure function (no I/O), which is good, but it returns the full mutated struct instead of a new typestate. It mutates in-place rather than returning a new immutable value.
findings.failure_mode: Callers may hold references to the pre-sent state and observe inconsistent data after mutation.
findings.fix: Return a new LedgerSent value constructed from the validated input. Do not mutate the input.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is decoupled from is_sent. A ledger can be is_sent=true with sent_at_epoch_ms=None, or is_sent=false with sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(...).
findings.failure_mode: Timestamp inconsistency breaks auditability — sent ledgers without timestamps, or timestamps without sent flag.
findings.fix: Bake sent_at_epoch_ms into the Sent variant: pub enum LedgerStatus { ..., Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }.
